Lal Behari Day

Twenty-two Bengali fairy tales of rākṣasas, ghosts, princes and clever jackals, as told by the women of a Bengal village, collected by Lal Behari Day (1883).

docs.title: About this book
docs.text:
Lal Behari Day (1824–1892), a Bengali writer and teacher, wrote down these tales as he had heard them as a child from the women of his village and from old storytellers, keeping their manner: tales of rākṣasas and the secret of their lives, of ghost-Brahmans and brahmadaityas, of the boy with the moon on his forehead and the match-making jackal. First published by Macmillan in 1883; the text of the illustrated edition of 1912.
